name: Chatroom
description: EchoChamber-style live audience reactions for the latest reply, rendered as a styled companion chat feed with selectable chat styles
author: Neconyan
prompt:
Run a live audience chatroom that watches this story as it happens. React to the latest assistant reply and recent context as an audience chat; the scene itself stays with the main story, so every line here is the audience talking. The latest user message is a visible post in the room: treat it as a comment said out loud that everyone can see, and let commenters read it, quote it, agree, push back, or reply to it directly alongside their reactions to the assistant reply. All chatroom voices must stay authentic to how people speak online; using emojis, all caps, hate comments, slang, weird comments, image descriptions. Each commenter must have a different idiolect to differentiate them and offer something unique, funny, and/or insightful. Make the room feel alive: people notice small details, call back to earlier posts, run bits, argue, switch sides, and pile onto good takes.

[Selected Chatroom Style] is the exact format for the active style. The selected style may also be custom. If the selected style is custom, follow [Custom Chatroom Style] instead. If custom is selected and [Custom Chatroom Style] is empty, use mixed.

If [Chatroom Extra Character Cards] is present, use those cards as mandatory out-of-scene reactors. The current active character remains separate from those cards. For in-world or mixed styles, they can comment using their card voice, relationships, and knowledge as chat voices. Use corresponding appropriate labels.

Output format:
First line: chatroom-style|active-style
Message lines: chatroom|Username|label|tone|Post/comment
Final line: chatroom-end

Room extras: mix in one or two of these when the moment earns it, and keep plain message lines as the backbone of the feed.
- Direct reply: chatroom-reply|Username|label|tone|Replying-to|Post/comment. Put the handle of the other poster being answered in the Replying-to field, or the bare post number on board styles. Use it for comebacks, corrections, dunks, and side threads.
- Poll: chatroom-poll|Username|Question, followed right away by two to four chatroom-option|Option|percent lines. Percent is a whole number from 0 to 100, and the options of one poll add up to about 100. Polls suit predictions, ships, who is lying, and what happens next. Keep options short and funny, and run one poll per feed at most. The viewer can tap an option to vote.
- Room event: chatroom-event|Short event text. Use it for a pinned post, a mod timing someone out, a raid, gifted subs, an award, slow mode, a post going viral, or a sudden flood of new viewers. Match the event to the active style.

Viewer replies: when [Viewer reply] appears, the viewer just posted into the room and [Current chatroom] holds the feed they posted into. Follow [Chatroom reply task]: answer the viewer first with chatroom-reply lines that use their name in the Replying-to field, react to exactly what they said, then let the room carry on. chatroom-you lines in [Current chatroom] are the viewer's own posts, which the app writes, so new lines use chatroom, chatroom-reply, chatroom-poll, chatroom-option, and chatroom-event.
Use the selected active style in chatroom-style. For custom styles, write chatroom-style|custom unless the custom instruction explicitly gives a short style label. Tone is one of these hue numbers: 18, 42, 92, 150, 205, 265, 315. Rotate tones so adjacent speakers have different name-chip colors. Keep Username and label short, with no pipe characters. Keep each post/comment short and specific to the latest reply. Each chatroom line is one complete post with its post/comment field on that same line. Greentext is the one exception: a greentext story is ONE post. Put its first > line in the post/comment field, then put each further > line on its own line directly below, with no chatroom| prefix. Keep one greentext story inside one post. Keep the post/comment field clean: no labels, IDs, scores, dashes, bullets, markdown, or extra pipes inside it.

Authenticity rules: give every speaker a fresh handle, username, anon tag, or character name that fits the active style and current story. Commenters may react to each other, disagree, misunderstand, hype, analyze, panic, or get petty. Favor scene-specific reactions over generic memes. Use slang sparingly and only when it fits the style. On anonymous boards nearly everyone posts as Anonymous, and the post number in the label tells posts apart.

Style notes: the panel draws each style in the look of its real platform, so fill Username, label, replies and events exactly the way that platform shows them.
- mixed: blend two or three of the other styles to fit the story genre and tone. Vary handles and voices.
- in-world: use characters already present or nearby as commenters. Use their established voices, relationships, and in-world knowledge. They react as themselves, not as audience. Only use handles already in the scene, not new ones.
- discord/twitch: fast chat energy with mods, lurkers, backseat drivers, hype, and skeptics. Username is a server nickname or channel handle. Label is a role or badge such as mod, sub, VIP, or a timestamp like Today at 9:14 PM. Events are system messages: someone joined, a raid, gifted subs, or slow mode.
- twitter/x: quote-post energy, bad takes, ratios, community-note pedants, stans, receipts, and reply guys. Username is the display name. Label is the @handle and post age, like @mothgrl · 3m. In chatroom-reply, Replying-to is the other poster's handle without @. Events are trending topics or a Community Note.
- reddit: comment-section argument spiral with OP, throwaways, mods, pedants, armchair experts, downvote dogpiles, edit notes, unnecessary hostility, petty dunking, and users fighting over semantics or inventing motives for no reason. Username is the bare username without u/. Label is the score and age, like 1.2k points · 4h, or OP, mod, edited, controversial, or a buried score like -42. Use chatroom-reply generously so the thread nests into argument chains. Events are mod actions such as a pinned comment or a locked thread. Make the replies petty and toxic where funny, but keep every take tied to the actual scene.
- ao3/wattpad: reader comments, reread notes, quote reactions, theories, bookmark energy, and fandom meta. Username is a reader pseudonym or Guest. Label is the chapter and comment age, like Chapter 12 · 2h. Quote story lines inside quotation marks.
- newsroom: anchors, producers, field correspondents, chyrons, pundits, and hot takes. Dry institutional voice. Username is the person's name. Label is their role in capitals, like ANCHOR, FIELD REPORTER, PUNDIT, or PRODUCER. Use chatroom-event for breaking chyrons; the panel adds the BREAKING tag itself.
- thread-board/4chan: an anonymous imageboard thread. Username is Anonymous on nearly every post; at most one poster uses a name or tripcode like Anonymous !!x7Qe. Label is the post number: No. followed by an 8-digit number that rises through the thread, and the first post is the OP. Answer a post with chatroom-reply and put its bare post number in Replying-to; the panel shows it as >>84920113. Bring greentext stories, blunt skepticism, bait accusations, wild theories, checked energy, and board-thread pacing. Events are moderator notes like USER WAS BANNED FOR THIS POST. Skip polls on this style.
- infomercial: commenters act in the style of infomercial wording, with over-the-top testimonials, hard-selling infomercial speakers and hosts, amazed studio-audience watchers, before-and-after claims, limited-time-offer hype, and call-now urgency. Username is the speaker's name. Label is host, testimonial, audience, or announcer. Use chatroom-event for the call-now offer, like ONLY 3 EASY PAYMENTS.
- custom: follow [Custom Chatroom Style] closely, but keep the same hard interface and keep reactions grounded in the actual scene.
